solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bumped into Harpo transformed as a figure of speech

parts.note: to have bumped into someone is to have met them

indicators.note: the letters of the name Harpo are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone ran into Harpo Marx, who had become a figure of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Harpo is one of the Marx Brothers, but here the name is just letters for 'transformed' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech that describes one thing as being another is the classic rhetorical device of comparison without 'like'.

clue.text: Valid ceasefire, the fourth to be abandoned

indicators.note: the fourth letter of the word for a ceasefire is dropped from it

parts.note: a ceasefire is a truce

explanation.surface: A ceasefire is declared valid, though the fourth party walks away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fourth to be abandoned' removes C, the fourth letter of TRUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something valid is correct or accurate, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Second journey for band

parts.note: a journey is a trip

explanation.surface: A band sets off on a second tour.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a long narrow piece of material, as is a strip of cloth or land.

clue.text: Eject with blaze in WW II fighter

parts.note: to spit is to eject from the mouth
a blaze is a fire

explanation.surface: A wartime fighter plane ejects its pilot as it goes up in flames.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spitfire was the famous British single-seat fighter aircraft of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Supermarine aircraft of that name is the best-known British fighter plane of the Second World War.

clue.text: Swift, heartless attack

indicators.note: the word for swift loses its central letter, its heart

parts.note: swift means rapid

explanation.surface: A swift and cruel assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes P, the middle letter of RAPID.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden surprise attack on an enemy or premises.

clue.text: Rustic getting round pound fine

indicators.note: the word for a rustic surrounds the abbreviation for pound

parts.note: a rustic is a country dweller, a peasant
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A countryman, collecting a pound, is quite content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting round' puts L inside PEASANT, after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine as in agreeable or nice, as of weather or company.

clue.text: Single large unit

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
one is the unit number

explanation.surface: A single big unit, as if from a price list.
explanation.definitionFit: Single and solitary mean the same: only one, by itself.

clue.text: Be cheerful — a result of hibernation ending?

definitions.meaning: to stay brave and in good spirits under difficulty
when hibernation ends, the animal that sleeps through winter gets up

explanation.surface: Cheer up: spring will bring winter's sleepers out.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a pun: the bear is up once its winter sleep ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to keep one's spirits up; read literally it pictures the hibernating animal on its feet.

clue.text: See king on throne

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: throne is jocular slang for a toilet, the loo
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Behold the king sitting on his throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throne' is not regal here: it is humorous British slang for the toilet, LOO.
explanation.definitionFit: To look is to direct the eyes, so a command to see is a command to behold.

clue.text: Regretted having left the last word initially to editor

parts.note: amen is the word that ends a prayer

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word to is taken

explanation.surface: An editor is sorry to have been left with the final say.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lamented something is to have mourned or expressed sorrow over it.

clue.text: Matured sage Derby shows it

indicators.note: the run of letters across sage Derby displays the answer inside it

explanation.surface: A cheese, Sage Derby, reveals how long it has matured.
explanation.walkthrough: Sage Derby is an English cheese flavoured with sage, which makes the surface about cheese-ripening.
explanation.definitionFit: Matured and grown old describe the same process, as with ripened cheese or wine.

clue.text: The best opportunity of risk beside the open ocean

indicators.note: the word for risk sits next to the ocean phrase, here after it

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the high seas
a chance is a risk

explanation.surface: A sailor sees the best chance in risking the high seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' for the open sea is old-fashioned, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the prime opportunity for advantage or profit, as in having an eye to it.

clue.text: Myself against myself? For the moment

parts.note: me is the speaker referring to themself
anti means against
me again, the speaker referring to themself

explanation.surface: A person at war with themself, for now at least.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb it means meanwhile, for the time being until something else happens.

clue.text: Waterfall is a problem for sightseers

definitions.meaning: a large steep cascade of water
an eye condition clouding the lens, troubling anyone who wants to see

explanation.surface: A great waterfall troubles tourists, perhaps by soaking them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sightseers' suggests tourists, but literally means anyone using their eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a big cascade and the clouding of the eye's lens that impairs vision.

clue.text: Secret codes let out

indicators.note: the letters of codes let are put out of order

explanation.surface: Secret codes have been leaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let out' reads as leaked; only 'out' is the anagram signal, rearranging CODESLET.
explanation.definitionFit: Closeted meetings are private and confidential, held behind closed doors.

clue.text: Mean onion tart cooked up for garnish?

indicators.note: the letters of mean onion tart are concocted into a new order

explanation.surface: A stingy onion tart is prepared as a garnish.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that garnish is an example of decoration, borrowed from the kitchen scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Garnish is decoration added to food, an instance of embellishment in general.

clue.text: Notice run overlooked in cricket, say

indicators.note: the run abbreviation is left out of the word for an example of cricket

parts.note: cricket is an example of a sport
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire observes a missed run.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to catch sight of or detect it.

clue.text: In favour of western front

parts.note: pro means in favour of

explanation.surface: Supporting the Western Front of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The forward part of a ship is its front end, cutting through the water.

clue.text: Kept area free for bird

indicators.note: the letters of kept area are released and set loose in another order

explanation.surface: An enclosure is freed of its captive bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small long-tailed parrot, a type of bird often kept as a pet.

clue.text: Examine carefully abandoning south-eastern land

indicators.note: the word for close examination gives up the compass abbreviation

parts.note: to peruse is to examine carefully

explanation.surface: A traveller studies the map, giving up on the south-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops SE from the end of PERUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Land in the sense of country, here the South American nation.

clue.text: Break up dislodging a piece of pavement

indicators.note: the letter a is knocked out of the reversed word
in a down clue the word break is read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: Breaking up the paving loosens a slab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses BREAK to KAERB; 'dislodging' then removes A.
explanation.definitionFit: The stone edging between road and footway, the raised edge of the sidewalk.

clue.text: Fitness is beneficial to millions

parts.note: something good for you is beneficial to you
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Getting fit is good for millions of people.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitness here is condition, as in an athlete or horse in good form.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in good condition, especially for sport, is a sense the word has in British usage.

clue.text: Tender after swallowing ecstasy and speed

indicators.note: the word for a tender takes in the drug letter

parts.note: to tend someone is to look after them, so a tender is a carer
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A nurse, having taken ecstasy and speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speed' looks like the drug but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush wildly at high velocity, as a runaway vehicle does.

clue.text: Clean back and front of tube that's burst

indicators.note: the word for clean is read back to front

parts.note: pure means clean

indicators.note: only the opening letter of tube is taken

explanation.surface: Cleaning the tube, back and front, after it has burst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses PURE to ERUP; 'front of' adds T.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst out suddenly, as a volcano or a violent quarrel does.
